solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Top Gear delighted guys (4,4)

blocks.note: to guy someone is to mock them, and so is to rag them

annotation.surface: A fan gushing that the motoring show Top Gear delighted its presenters.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals dress up the definition as the TV motoring show; read plainly, top gear is your best clothes, which is what glad rags are. 'Guys' is a verb here, not the men.
annotation.definitionFit: Glad rags are your finest clothes, the top gear you put on for a party.

entries.clue: Pregnancy one had through physical attraction (9)

indicatorNotes.through: I'D runs through the middle of GRAVITY, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: gravity is the physical force of attraction between masses
'I had' contracts to I'D, with I = one

annotation.surface: A pregnancy blamed on a purely physical attraction.
annotation.walkthrough: Gravidity is the medical word for pregnancy, from Latin gravidus, heavy. 'Physical' reads as bodily lust but points to physics.
annotation.definitionFit: Gravidity is the state of being pregnant, a medical term.

entries.clue: Old queen given the chop wanting head stuck on (7)

indicatorNotes.wanting head: wanting = lacking, so AXED lacks its first letter

blocks.note: given the chop = AXED, minus its first letter A

annotation.surface: An old queen beheaded, the head still needing to be stuck back on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all executions, but the chop and the head are both working at letter level: the head that goes is the A of AXED.
annotation.definitionFit: Something annexed has been added or attached, stuck on to something larger.

entries.clue: Unusual Vermeer: thorned head dedicated to Christ (8,6)

indicatorNotes.Unusual: the letters appear in an unusual order

annotation.surface: An odd Vermeer painting of a thorn-crowned head of Christ.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a religious painting with a crown of thorns; the definition is instead the head of a convent, a woman dedicated to Christ.
annotation.definitionFit: A Reverend Mother is the head of a community of nuns, who are dedicated to Christ.

entries.clue: Old Irishmen among others from the south hated cops (7)

indicatorNotes.from the south: in a down entry, read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Pat is the stock Irishman's name
e.g. = exempli gratia, for example, among others

annotation.surface: Old Irishmen, among others from the south, hated the police.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Among others' looks like a container instruction, but it is simply E.G. The whole string is then turned upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: The Gestapo were the Nazi secret police, a hated force.

entries.clue: Slow mover fails to finish in scheduled time (4)

indicatorNotes.fails to finish: the word stops short of its last letter

blocks.note: a slow mover is a SLOTH, minus its last letter H

annotation.surface: A slowcoach who does not finish in the allotted time.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a race result; the sloth is the slow mover and it is the word, not the animal, that fails to finish.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from broadcasting and booking: the period set aside for something in a timetable.

entries.clue: Minor water leak affected tenancy (7)

indicatorNotes.affected: the letters of LEAK are affected, altered in their order

blocks.note: a let is a tenancy, as in a short let

annotation.surface: A small leak of water damaging a tenancy, a landlord's complaint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minor water' reads as a small leak in the surface, but it is the definition: a little lake.
annotation.definitionFit: A lakelet is a small lake, a minor body of water.

entries.clue: Twinkling star aircrew noted at certain frequency (5)

indicatorNotes.noted at certain frequency: letters are noted only at a regular interval, every second one

annotation.surface: A twinkling star spotted by an aircrew.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twinkling' looks like it describes the star, but it is the definition, as in 'in a twinkling'. 'Frequency' is not about radio.
annotation.definitionFit: In a trice and in a twinkling both mean in an instant.

entries.clue: Before parking, regarding clamps? (2,10,2)

indicatorNotes.clamps: the longer phrase clamps round P, holding it inside

blocks.note: P = parking, as on road signs

annotation.surface: A question about parking and wheel clamps.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about wheel clamps, but 'clamps' is the instruction. 'Before' means 'rather than', as in 'death before dishonour'.
annotation.definitionFit: To choose one thing before another is to choose it in preference to the other.

entries.clue: Driving instructor placed vehicle in reverse (6)

indicatorNotes.in reverse: VAN is put in reverse, read backwards

blocks.note: to sit something somewhere is to place it: sat = placed

annotation.surface: A driving instructor puts the car into reverse gear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Driving instructor' suggests a person teaching learners; it is the gadget that tells you where to drive. Satnav is short for satellite navigation.
annotation.definitionFit: A satnav instructs the driver where to go, turn by turn.

entries.clue: Old Indian’s tongue Romeo pierces without tools for the job (8)

indicatorNotes.pierces: R pierces KIT, ending up inside it

blocks.note: a kit is a set of tools for a job
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: An old Indian's tongue pierced by Romeo, who had no tools to do it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' means language, and 'Romeo' is a letter, not a lover.
annotation.definitionFit: Sanskrit is the ancient classical language of India.

entries.clue: Cross after Jack admitted reason for loss of fortune? (4)

indicatorNotes.after: 'after' in its sense of 'following in order': the cross is written following Jack and 'admitted'

blocks.note: J = jack, in a pack of cards

annotation.surface: A card player cross that the jack let in lost them their fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fortune' is luck rather than money, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A jinx is a curse that brings bad luck, a cause of lost fortune.

entries.clue: Earl or lord given makeover way smoother? (10)

indicatorNotes.given makeover: the letters are made over into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An aristocrat getting a makeover to become a smoother operator.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Way smoother' suggests a suave nobleman; it is the machine that smooths roads, with 'way' meaning road.
annotation.definitionFit: A roadroller flattens and smooths the surface of a road, or way.

entries.clue: Pacific island recreated in opening of Disney’s Moana (8)

indicatorNotes.recreated: the letters are created again in a new order
indicatorNotes.opening of: the opening of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A Pacific island recreated for the opening scenes of the Disney film Moana, set in Polynesia.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits nicely, since Moana is itself set on a Pacific island. Mindanao is the large southern island of the Philippines.
annotation.definitionFit: Mindanao is the second-largest island of the Philippines, in the western Pacific.

entries.clue: Obsession leads to feelings evoking trauma somewhat? (6)

indicatorNotes.leads to: the leads of the words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Feelings Evoking Trauma

annotation.surface: A psychologist's note that an obsession brings on feelings that echo a trauma.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leads to' reads as 'causes' in the surface; here it picks out the leading letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the psychological sense: a fixation on one object or practice that crowds out everything else.

entries.clue: Empty such a barrel full of beer quickly, please (5,1,3)

indicatorNotes.Empty: an emptied word loses its insides, keeping only its outer letters
indicatorNotes.full of: the barrel is full of the beer, holding it inside

blocks.note: a keg is a small barrel

annotation.surface: An order to drain a barrel full of beer, and fast.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a pub landlord in a hurry. 'Shake a leg!' is an order to hurry up, so the definition is the whole urging phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Shake a leg! means hurry up, a request to be quick.

entries.clue: Total pain swapping plaster, essentially (6)

indicatorNotes.swapping: the two words swap places, so the second comes first

blocks.note: gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'

annotation.surface: A plasterer complaining that changing the plaster was a total pain.
annotation.walkthrough: Gyp is British slang for pain. 'Essentially' makes the definition fair: gypsum is the essential ingredient of plaster.
annotation.definitionFit: Gypsum is the mineral from which plaster of Paris is made, plaster in essence.

entries.clue: Like the arctic winter? Start to shiver, if not (7)

indicatorNotes.Start to: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: The arctic winter will make you shiver, if nothing else.
annotation.walkthrough: In the depths of the arctic winter the sun never rises, hence the question mark on an example definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The arctic winter has days when the sun never rises, so it is sunless.

entries.clue: Opening top, appreciate man spending millions on Ferrari? (8)

indicatorNotes.spending millions: the man spends his M, so it is gone

blocks.note: a Ferrari is an example of a car
to dig something is to appreciate it

annotation.surface: A rich man splashing out millions on a Ferrari with an opening top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening top' reads as a convertible roof, which suits the Ferrari; it is a knitted top that opens down the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a knitted top that buttons open down the front.

entries.clue: Locating neckwear, dicky bow, in locked room (7)

indicatorNotes.dicky: dicky = unsound, faulty, so the letters are out of order
indicatorNotes.in: the letters go in the room

blocks.note: a cell is a locked room

annotation.surface: Hunting for a neck accessory, a dicky bow, in a locked room.
annotation.walkthrough: A dicky bow is British slang for a bow tie, and the surface wants it as the neckwear; 'dicky' is the instruction. The definition is cryptic: a bell on a cow's neck lets the herder locate it.
annotation.definitionFit: A cowbell hangs round a cow's neck so its owner can locate it by the sound.

entries.clue: Muslim married on board cruise going from island to island (7)

indicatorNotes.on board: M is taken on board SAIL, inside it
indicatorNotes.going from island to island: the result runs from one I to another I

annotation.surface: A married Muslim taking a cruise that hops between islands.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ismailis are a branch of Shia Islam, led by the Aga Khan.
annotation.definitionFit: An Ismaili is a member of a Shia Muslim sect.

entries.clue: Tug with replacement coming around will probably land (5,2,3)

indicatorNotes.coming around: the replacement comes around TOW, enclosing it

annotation.surface: A tugboat with a relief crew coming round will probably make land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Land' sounds like reaching shore, which suits the tug; it means win, as in landing a prize or a bet.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'stand to' means be in a position to, and 'land' is the informal sense of secure or win, as in landing a contract.

entries.clue: Health done for? (5)

blocks.note: a health is a drink raised to someone's wellbeing, as in 'drink his health'
done for = finished, ruined, in modern slang

annotation.surface: A question whether someone's health is finished.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers both meanings: a health drunk to someone, and slang for finished.
annotation.definitionFit: A toast is a health drunk to someone; being toast means being done for.

entries.clue: Look average to the audience (4)

indicatorNotes.to the audience: what the audience hears is the sound, not the spelling

annotation.surface: A performer looking merely average to the audience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look' is a noun here, a person's bearing or expression.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, a literary one: the look of a person's face and bearing that shows their mood or character.

entries.clue: Withdraw before explosive parents snap! (4,4)

indicatorNotes.Withdraw: to withdraw is to draw back, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A child telling someone to back off before their parents explode and snap at them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Snap!' is the cry when two things match, as in the card game Snap, so it means 'me too'. 'Withdraw' looks like the definition but reverses everything after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Saying 'snap!' on noticing a match is like saying 'same here'.

entries.clue: Emend good book deleting one TB, for consumption (6)

indicatorNotes.deleting: the letters I, T and B are deleted

blocks.note: to emend a text is to edit it
the Good Book is the Bible
one = I; that I, a T and a B are the letters deleted from EDIT and BIBLE

annotation.surface: An editor emending a medical book, cutting a passage on TB, or consumption.
annotation.walkthrough: Consumption is an old name for TB, so the surface pairs them; in the definition it just means eating.
annotation.definitionFit: Something edible is fit for consumption, safe to eat.

entries.clue: Cobblers not all into shoes (4)

indicatorNotes.not all: only part of the words is used

annotation.surface: Not all cobblers work on shoes.
annotation.walkthrough: Cobblers is British slang for nonsense, and tosh means the same; the surface uses the shoe-mender sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Tosh and cobblers are both British slang for nonsense.

entries.clue: Book soon to come out (8)

blocks.note: B = book, as in the abbreviation for a volume
something looming is about to happen, soon to come

annotation.surface: A book due to be published soon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come out' reads as publication, suiting the book, but the definition is just 'out', as flowers are out when in bloom.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the garden: flowers that are out are open, in bloom.
